morphology.shape: Curved/comma-shaped rod, sometimes S-shaped or gull-wing pairs
morphology.motility: Motile with a single polar flagellum, characteristic darting motility

habitat.naturalHabitat: GI tract of birds and mammals
habitat.hostAssociation: Commensal in poultry gut; pathogenic in humans

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative curved/comma or S-shaped rods, "gull-wing" pairs

culture.media: Campy-selective (Skirrow's, Campy-CVA) agar, 42°C incubation, microaerophilic atmosphere

identificationClues: Grows selectively at 42°C under microaerophilic conditions
Hippurate hydrolysis distinguishes from C. coli

virulenceFactors: Lipooligosaccharide (molecular mimicry linked to Guillain-Barré syndrome)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral; undercooked poultry is the most common source, also unpasteurized milk and contaminated water
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common bacterial causes of gastroenteritis worldwide; leading antecedent infection associated with Guillain-Barré syndrome
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Requires special microaerophilic incubation at 42°C on selective media — not recovered on routine stool culture media

examFacts.importantTest: Selective culture at 42°C under microaerophilic conditions
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Thermophilic growth at 42°C and microaerophilic requirement distinguish it from most enteric pathogens
